itemized_evaluation.justification: The paper includes explicit conflict of interest and funding disclosures in the Declarations section: 'Competing interests. D.S. is the founder and a beneficiary of FreshCredit Inc. and the founder of The FreshCredit Lab. FreshCredit Inc holds granted US utility patents... Funding. None received; independent research.'

The paper is an un-reviewed preprint ('The companion theory preprint defines trust...', 'OSF / Zenodo Archive (Release v4.3, Accession: https://github.com/devonshigaki/trust-stack-research-collection/releases/tag/v4.3)') with no documented peer-review credentials or reputable journal publication.

Prior literature is represented with rigorous balance and without selective framing, explicitly detailing negative results and controversies: e.g., §2.2 'Against the “trust molecule” framing: the foundational intranasal-oxytocin trust effect is dead... d = 0.077, 95% CI [-0.124, 0.278], p = .45', §2.5 'The contrary evidence, which must be cited with it...', and §4.4 'The contested status must now be stated as plainly as the hypothesis, because the demolitions are substantial...'.

The paper establishes a reproducible protocol with exact seeds, byte-verified checkpoints, and open code: 'The released TRIBE v2 checkpoint (facebook/tribev2 best.ckpt) was verified byte-exactly for this work — exactly 708,856,138 bytes... Repeat inference is bit-exact (max |Δ| = 0.0)' and 'All simulation code, seeds, formal SMT proofs, high-resolution figures, and pre-registration documents are permanently deposited... with cryptographic SHA-256 manifest verification'.

Sampling selection bias is explicitly controlled in connectome analyses via uniform random sampling ('A frozen uniform sample of 12,000 post-synaptic roots (seed 45; 8,256 class-typed...)', §5.7) and author-selection bias in concept sets is explicitly identified and remedied with a blinded rater protocol ('The concept sets below are author-selected, with no independent coder, and both facts are stated as limitations... The author-selection limitation of §4.6... now has a specified remedy, pre-registered before rating begins: minimum three independent raters per artifact... blind to the framework’s hypotheses', §4.6, §5.2).

Explicit power calculations and sample size justifications are provided for the experimental protocol in §5.1: 'N = 60 enrolled -> 48 completers (20% multi-session attrition)... Power at N = 48: 0.78–0.92 for the per-probe test at d_z = 0.5–0.6 (alpha = 0.01, Bonferroni over five confirmatory tests...) and 0.92 for the pooled test at d_z = 0.5, alpha = 0.05' as well as large simulation samples (e.g., N = 10,000 sessions in §5.18; N = 2,000,000 Monte Carlo draws in §5.33).

The experimental protocols use double-blinding and proper controls (§5.1: 'DOCAS-GATE-1: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, within-subject crossover with 7 sessions per participant'; §5.2: 'minimum three independent raters per artifact... blind to the framework’s hypotheses'), and all in-silico simulations employ explicit negative controls (e.g., §5.3 'shuffled-mixing-matrix null yields r = 0.054', §5.5 'E3 — shuffling the update stream... destroys the law in 200/200 negative-control replicates').

Appropriate statistical tests are paired with explicit effect sizes and practical significance discussions across the paper: e.g., Mantel tests with r values (§1.1 'Mantel r = 0.252 (cortical) and 0.240 (embedding)... far below any isometry claim'), ANOVA with eta-squared (§5.18 'F(3, 9996) = 3,561.48, p < 10^-15, large effect size eta^2 = 0.5166'), Cohen's d (§5.24 'Cohen's d = 2.79'), and odds ratios (§4.2 'OR = 0.89', §5.4 'odds ratio OR_D1/D10 = 38.94').

Randomization seeds, counterbalancing schemes, and agent/population allocations are thoroughly detailed: e.g., §5.1 'session order counterbalanced by a Williams-balanced assignment over the six probes (48 = 8 x 6 preserves the balance), with the placebo session at a fixed position', and exact random seeds and population distributions specified for every simulation (e.g., §5.13 'N = 1,000 heterogeneous agents, kappa_i ~ Beta(2, 5), seed 42').

Exact p-values, confidence intervals, standard errors, and correlation metrics are consistently reported: e.g., §2.2 'd = 0.077, 95% CI [-0.124, 0.278], p = .45', §4.2 'p = 5.39 x 10^-11, OR = 0.89 (95% CI 0.86–0.92)... p = .18, OR = 0.97 (95% CI 0.93–1.02)', and §5.14 'beta_IVW(ADCY8) = 0.2284 (SE = 0.0223, p = 2.4 x 10^-24)'.

Baseline metrics and raw counts are systematically reported alongside relative percentages and ratios: e.g., §4.6 '0.267 (12/45 edges)... 0.000 (0/15 edges)', §5.4 '114 of 196 battery content words mapped to Concepticon nodes (tiered matching fully logged: 52 exact gloss, 19 morphological, 43 via an explicit documented synonym table... 82 unmapped)', and §5.17 '1.7% baseline emergency uptake... accepted by 95.7% of agents under multimodal cloaking... D_1... 16.12x relative to the top decile (D_10, 98.0% vs. 75.2% uptake)'.

Attrition, indeterminate runs, unmapped items, and corrupted data exclusions are fully logged and accounted for: e.g., §5.1 'N = 60 enrolled -> 48 completers (20% multi-session attrition)... a session failing engagement is excluded from that row of M and reported', §5.6 'INDETERMINATE outcomes are reported, never dropped', and §5.7 'Four disclosed amendments accompanied execution (including a corrected cell-type map rebuilt from the authoritative annotation table after a provenance-corrupted artifact was detected and retired...)'.

The paper explicitly distinguishes between surrogate/proxy measurements and true biological endpoints, refusing to swap them: e.g., Abstract 'All in-silico evidence reported here is instrument-level: no neurochemistry was measured anywhere in this paper', and §5 'It tests pipeline decodability and separable channel signatures, not the carrier mapping — HRV, sleep, and activity measures are several inference steps from neuromodulatory tone and cannot distinguish the named carriers; pharmacological or PET-level perturbation is the actual gate for carrier claims'.

Statistical significance is strictly separated from practical/construct validity and magnitude: e.g., §4.6 'the N.3 category-LOO decode survives every correction while being a known artifact (templatic lexicon; the semantic-only control also decodes at 1.000) — multiplicity correction controls the false-positive rate, not construct validity', and §1.1 'it is partially supported at effect sizes far below any isometry claim (§4.6, §5.2)'.

Correlation is explicitly prevented from being presented as causation, and confounding variables (such as LD, pleiotropy, and open-label expectancy) are addressed: e.g., §4.7 'Because no tier is causal and the genetic tiers substantially re-descend from circular legacy genetics, this triangulation licenses no causal claim', §5.4 'outputs are associations among model predictions until human concordance data exist, and the correlation–causation discipline of the Supporting Document (§S.3–S.4) governs every claim', and §5.8 'flags expectancy as the principal confound of the open-label design'.

Only figure legends and HTML image placeholders (e.g., '') are present in the provided text; the actual visual graphs cannot be inspected to verify baseline starting points or un-distorted axes, and the text itself notes in 'Figure legends' that several figures ('Figure 1... Figure 3... Figure 6') have no deposited image files.

Hypotheses and criteria were pre-registered and frozen prior to execution, failed criteria are reported as failures without post-hoc threshold moving, and post-hoc explorations are explicitly segregated: e.g., §4.6 '6 of the 13 BH survivors are post-hoc assemblies... disclosed in each case... post-hoc tests that survive correction remain post-hoc for hypothesis-generation weight', §5.5 'E2 — the failure, stated plainly: the framework failed its pre-registered double-dissociation criterion as frozen... The failure is not re-narrated as support. What follows is post-hoc hypothesis generation, labeled as such.'

No real longitudinal follow-up of human participants has been executed; the paper consists of in-silico simulations and a pre-registered protocol pending future execution ('no neurochemistry was measured anywhere in this paper... human in-vivo pharmacological validation (DOCAS-GATE-1) is fully pre-registered and pending clinical trial execution', Abstract; 'No human data are reported', Declarations).

The paper explicitly bounds its mathematical models and tests where linear approximations break down rather than extrapolating beyond data ranges: e.g., §4.6 'Single words are, however, out-of-distribution input for instruments trained on naturalistic narrative... these models’ representational geometry is stimulus-class-sensitive', §3 'dominance = d(Δτ)/dt... its value remains sampling-rate dependent — cross-condition and cross-study comparisons are meaningful only at matched sampling rates', and §5.33 'Near equilibrium (ε = r - r_e -> 0), the quantum restoring force linearizes... Under severe shear displacement exceeding the dissociation energy (ε > r_yield), the restoring force vanishes'.

The entire architecture is built around enforcing biological and mathematical plausibility: e.g., Abstract 'Because the five neuromodulatory systems involved operate on timescales spanning more than four orders of magnitude (0.1 s to ~2,700 s)... no serial five-step cascade is physiologically coherent. DOCAS is therefore framed here as a parallel, multi-timescale modulation architecture', §2.4 'catecholamines do not cross the blood–brain barrier: circulating epinephrine cannot be the carrier of a central activation signal', and §2.9 'The component-wise non-negative vector a(t)... is what the theory’s Fisher–Rao construction normalizes into the stage-mix simplex coordinate θ'.
